claims.text: The current HVAF-i7 feedstock is FeCoNiCrAl powder in the 15–45 μm size range.
The existing HVAF-i7 baseline produces acceptable coating quality but insufficient coating thickness.
Setting the HVAF-i7 spray distance to approximately 300–350 mm constitutes a reduction relative to the current setting.
Reducing the HVAF-i7 spray distance to approximately 300–350 mm increases particle impact velocity and kinetic energy.
Reducing the spray distance will overcome the FeCoNiCrAl coating-thickness limitation.
A shorter spray distance reduces in-flight particle cooling.
A shorter spray distance reduces in-flight oxidation of the particles.
Spray distance affects the oxide content of deposited high-entropy-alloy coatings.
Higher particle kinetic energy improves particle melting.
Higher particle velocity and kinetic energy improve deposition efficiency.
Improved deposition efficiency increases material build-up and coating thickness.
The adjusted spray distance will produce a significantly thicker coating than the current 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline.
The adjusted spray distance will improve coating adhesion relative to the baseline.
The adjusted spray distance will maintain minimal as-sprayed oxidation and the desired oxidation resistance.
The intervention will remain effective for substrates with internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The resulting coating will remain effective during elevated-temperature thermal-barrier service.
Changes in powder properties or extreme geometrical constraints may alter the intervention's effectiveness.
Oxidation during spraying can change residual particle composition and destabilize phases, creating possible microstructural trade-offs.
A controlled experiment will compare spray distances of 200, 300, 350, and 400 mm while holding all other deposition parameters constant.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant increase in thickness exceeding 20% at 300–350 mm, or the occurrence of unacceptable oxidation or adhesion, will falsify the hypothesis.
